Mr. Mainul Hosein with Mr. Joynul Abedin, Advocates ------ For the Appellant. 
Mr. S. B. Barua, Advocates ------ For the State.
parties:
Anwar Ali ------ Petitioner
Vs

full_judgment:
Fazle Hussain Mohammad Habibur Rahman, J:-Accused-Appellant Md. Anwar Ali was tried in absentia and convicted u/s 16 (3) read with section 16(1)(a) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 by Mr. Afzalul Huq, Special Tribunal, Pabna on 7.2.87 in Special Tribunal case No. 27/85 and sentenced to suffer R.I. for 3 years and to pay a fine of Tk. 7,00,000/- in default, to suffer R.I. for 1 year more. The sentence passed shall run from the date of his apprehension. The amount of fine shall be realised by attachment or sale of moveable property standing in his name and the name of his wife or in the name of his benamdar. The accused-appellant surrendered to custody and executed vokalatnama on 7.4.87 and preferred this appeal on 2.5.87. 

 2. The case for the prosecution, in short, is that Mrs. Akhtar Monjura Begum as Managing Director M/S. M.A. Rashid, Abdul Majid Khan, A.B. Siddique, M.A. Jalil and Md. Jafrul Huq as Directors of M/S. Decent Oil Mills Ltd. Pabna applied for loan to the then Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan (now Bangladesh Shilpa Bank) for a loan in foreign exchange (Deutsche Marks) and local currency and the then Industrial Development Bank (now Bangladesh Shilpa Bank) sanctioned D.M. 83,220/ (equivalent to Rs (now Tk.) 99,000/- in foreign currency and Rs. (now Tk.) 30,000/00 in local currency. The credit agreement between the Industrial Development Bank (now Bangladesh Shilpa Bank) and M/S. Decent Oil Mills Ltd. in respect of the foreign currency loan of the said amount of Tk. 99,000/- was executed on 13th August 1968 while the credit agreement in respect of the local currency loan of Tk. 30,000/- between the said parties was executed on 10th September, 1970. The loan in foreign currency was for setting up of a Linseed Oil extracting plant at Small Industries Corporation Industrial Estate, Pabna for producing crude Linseed Oil and Oil Cake. The local currency loan was sanctioned for the construction of the factory building. The machineries mentioned in the schedule were mortgaged. The Managing Director of the said M/S Decent Oil Mills Ltd. executed the credit agreement, D.P. notes agreements creating mortgage and hypothecation, irrecoverable general power of attorney in favour of the bank, mortgaging assets and machineries of the company in lieu of the said loan. The said company took the loan money. The foreign currency loan was to be repaid in 18 half yearly installments within 10 years starting from the date of opening their letter of credit or as per amortization schedule of credit and the local currency loan was to, be repaid by 9 half yearly installments within 5 years. The rate of interest was 7-1/2% per annum on the entire amount of foreign currency loan together with the other charges at bank's usual rate. The rate of interest for the local currency loan was 7% per annum payable at 1/2 yearly rates. In spite of repeated reminders by the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank M/S Decent Oil Mills Ltd. and its Directors failed to repay the said loan with interest which amounted to Tk. 6,59,444/58 as on 28.2.78 and the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank under Article 33 of P.O. No. 129/72 filed Misc. Case No. 40/ 78 against M/S Decent Oil Mills Ltd., B.S.C.I.C. Industrial Estate. Pabna and its 7 Directors for realisation of the said dues and also for realisation of damages and interest till the realisation of the total amount due to the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank. The District Judge, Pabna by his order dated 13-5-78 passed ad-interim order of attachment of the machineries of the said Oil Mill. The court through its officer on 19.5.78 physically attached the machineries and the ad interim order of attachment was made absolute on 24.2.79. The District Judge, Pabna decreed the Miscellaneous Case in favour of the Shilpa Bank on 1.9.79 for the said dues with interest till recovery by auction sale of the attached property. Accused appellant Md. Anwar Ali in his name and in the name of his wife Nurun Nahar Beg giving their address to he 301, Khalishpur B.I.D.C. Road, Khulna had purchased all the shares of the Directors Pabna on the 1st and 2nd February, 1979 and in that capacity he appeared in the above case in the court of the District Judge and applied to be added as a party, but his application was rejected. When Mr. Karim, Manager. Bangladesh shilpa Bank, Pabna and Mr. A. Razzaque. Advocate and Legal Advisor of the Shipa Bank were allegedly making preparation to start an execution case for executing the decree, accused Md. Anwar Ali approached the Manager Mr. Karim and verbally promised to satisfy the decretal dues of the Shilpa Bank through negotiations amicably and undertook to send a bank draft of Tk. 50,000/- in favout of Bangladesh Shilpa Bank. When accused Anwar Ali failed to comply with his commitment with the bank (the accused actually deposited Tk. 55,000/- in Shilpa Bank on 24.6.81), the said Manager visited (after about of attachment) the project site of M/S Decent Oil Mills Ltd. In B.S.C.I.C. Industrial Estate, Pabna for physical verification of the attached property (in the month of September, 81) and found that said accused Md. Anwar Ali with his laborers was setting up a new prject “Screen Printing and finishing unit” in the self-same project site of M/S Decent Oil Mills Ltd. But did not find the machineries of the Oil Mills. On his query the accused appellant stated that the machineries of the Oil Mills had been sent to Khulna for the purpose of repairing the would be brought back soon at its original site in the premises. The accused appellant with the help of the members of his staff had removed and taken away the said attached machineries some time after June, 1981. The accused appellant thus dishonestly for unlawful gain committed theft and misappropriated the attached machineries worth Tk. 10,00,000/- (Taka ten lacs) which were mortgaged to the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank. Accused Anwar Ali as the co-owner of M/S. Decent Oil Mills Ltd., Pabna thus, according to the first charge-sheet submitted by the prosecution committed offences punishable u/s 403 and 380 of the Penal Code. The local Manager of Shilpa Bank by his Memo No. 1603 dated 15.1.82 sent complaint to O.C. Pabna P.S. who sent it to the District Anti-Corruption Bureau. Mr. Md. Dabiruddin, Assistant Inspector, District Anti-Corruption Bureau, Pabna lodged a written F.I.R. with the Pabna P.S. on 31.3.83 giving the time of commission of theft and misappropriation to be between 27.4.68 to 31.7.80. After investigation informant Mr. Dabiruddin, Assistant Inspector District Anti Corruption Bureau, Pabna lodged a written F.I.R. with the Pabna P.S. on 31.3.83 giving the time of commission of theft and misappropriation to be between 27.4.68 to 31.7.80. After investigation informant Mr. Dabiruddin, Assistant Inspector, District Anti Compton Bureau, Pabna submitted the first charge sheet against accused Md. Anwar Ali on 29.6.83 u/s 406 and 380 of the Penal Code. Subsequently the Manager, Shilpa Bank and the Legal Adviser, Shilpa Bank, Pabna preferred a motion before the Sessions Judge, Pabna submitting that this offence should be tried u/s 15 and 16 of the Special Powers Act instead of trying the accused u/ss. 406 and 380 of the Penal Code. The Additional Sessions Judge, Pabna directed the police (other than any D.A.B. Office) to reinvestigate the case under the Special Powers Act. After the Sub-Inspector of Police submitted supplementary charge sheet (under the order of the court of Sessions) under sections 15 and 16 of the Special Powers Act on 24.8.85 the Special Tribunal, Pabna took cognizance of the offence on 17.9.85 and it was numbered as Special Case No. 27 of 1985. Accused Anwar moved the Criminal Revision No. 137 of 1985 before the Rangpur Bench of the High Court Division u/s 561A Cr.P.C. for quashing the Criminal Proceedings. The Division Bench at Rangpur summarily rejected the application on 18.11.85. After being released on ad interim bail the accused continued to abscond from 19.11.85 in spite of orders passed by the Tribunal to secure his attendance in the court of the Special Tribunal. At the time of trial in absentia Mr. M.A. Haque, the Special Tribunal, Pabna after cancelling the earlier charge framed on 8.12.86 that the offence was committed by the accused appellant between 3.12.86 and 7.11.87, ultimately on 8.1.87 framed the following charge against the absconding accused Anwar Ali :- 

 "You at any time between 1.6.81 and 9.9.81 at B.S.C.I.C. Industrial Estate, Pabna within P. S. and District Pabna with the dishonest intention to prejudice the economic or financial interest of the State, removed by taking out of the possession and disposed of the machineries of Decent Oil Mills Ltd. viz (1) 10 Komet Double spindle Oil Expellors, (2) 2 System Feeding Pipes with collection Box and Throttles Vulves for feeding seeds to each expelling machines, D.D.-85 and spare parts thereof such as a) 5 worms b) 5 Cyclinders c) 3 Plungers 3)3 Prsssing Heads and e) 10 Ball bearings worth in all Tk. 10,00,000/- which were under mortgage with the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank and were under attachment of the Court of the District Judge, Pabna in connection with Misc, Case No. 40/78 and you there by committed prejudicial act intending or likely to prejudicial act intending or likely to prejudice the economic or financial interests of the State an offence Punishable under Section 16(3) read with Section 16(1) (a) of the Special Powers Act. 1974". 

 "Shilpa Bank brought this (Misc.) case (Misc. Case No. 40 of 1979) against the Decent Oil Mill Ltd. and its (original) directors for realisation of outstanding dues of Tk. 6,59,444/58 poisha as on 28.2.78 against the said loan. This accused Anwar Ali by stating to have purchased the shares of all the directors of the Decent Oil Mill Ltd. applied to be a party in that Misc. Case on 8.5.79, but it was rejected and the Misc. Case was decreed for the said sum ex parte. From Ext. 3 (letter dated 29.6.81 written by P.W. 1 Mr. M.M. Karim, Manager of the Pabna Branch of the Shilpa Bank addressed to the A.G.M., Legal Department, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank, Head Office, Dhaka) we do find that the said accused Anwar Ali (by demand drafts Nos. 8810 and 8811) on 24.6.81 deposited a sum of Tk. 55,000/- (i.e. Tk. 50,000/- plus Tk. 5,000/-) against the total dues which was forwarded to the Head Office by the local Shilpa Bank for necessary action. Be the case as it may, we find from Ext. 5 series and 2 that accused Anwar Ali and wife (Nurun Nahar Begum) in February, 1979, purchased the shares of the original Directors of the Decent Oil Mill Ltd. and got their names mutated in the office of the Registrar of the Joint Stock Company. From Ext 3/1 dated 9.3.82 (a letter written by the Manager, Legal Department, Shilpa Bank, Dhaka addressed to accused Md. Anwar Ali) we find that accused Anwar Ali was informed to pay the decretal dues. From Ext. 3/2 (dated nil) we find that accused Anwar Ali reported to the Manager, Shilpa Bank that the building and godown of the Millon being damaged by cyclone he constructed new boundary wall and shifted all machineries of the Oil Mill elsewhere. From Ext. 6, letter dated 10.2.86 written by Nurunnahar Begum (wife of the accused) to the Managing Director, Shilpa Bank, Head Office, Dhaka we find that his wife (Nurunnahar Begum) (who) got her name registered as Managing Director reported to the Shilpa Bank that her husband shifted the machineries of the Decent Oil Mill to Dalutpur, Khulna (for repair but could not be repaired). The informant P.W.I, the then Manager Mr. Karim has said that since accused Anwar Ali could no longer be contacted, he under the instruction of the Head Office had to submit a written complaint to the O.C., Pabna P.S. (It is significant to note that the Special Tribunal has nowhere in his judgment taken into consideration the fact that both P.W.1, Mr. Karim, the then Manager, Inspection and Evaluation Department, Headquarter, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank, Dhaka and P.W.6 M.A. Razzak, Legal Advisor of the Pabna Branch of the Shilpa Bank deposed without telling the date of visit that they visited the Decent Oil Mill together, found no machineries there and that on query accused Anwar Ali told that he had sent the machineries to Khulna for repair) P.W.2 Ashish Kumar Kundu and P.W.3 Rafiqul Hasan are attesting witnesses of the relevant documents (which) I.O. seized from the Shilpa Bank, Pabna, under seizure list Ext. 7. P.W.4 Syed Kabir Hossain, Sheristadar, has said that the I.O. seized the record of the Misc. Case No. 40 of 1978 under seizure list Ext. 8 P.W.7 Mr. Khan, the present Manager of the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank, Pabna has produced various relevant documents from the Bank Ext. 9 series. From all these documentary evidence we do find that accused Anwar Ali came into the scene and it is he who dishonestly removed the attached machineries of the Decent Oil Mill from its premises from B.S.C.I.C. Industrial Area, Pabna and misappropriated it and thereby committed prejudicial act within the meaning of clause (f)(viii) of section 2 of the Special Powers Act (Act XIV of 1974) and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 16(3) of the Special Powers Act. Before I part. (with this case) I would like to say a few words as to the conduct displayed by this accused. He was allowed to go on bail just to facilitate to move the Hon'ble High Court against the order of this court allowing a Misc. case for further investigation. He did it, but the Hon'ble High Court rejected his application summarily. In the result of further investigation when the Investigating Agency submitted fresh (supplementary) charge sheet he once again was allowed to go on bail on his prayer to move the Hon'ble High Court and since then he has been absconding. All these acts of his plus the recourse he took by stepping into the Decent Oil Mill Ltd. lend assurance to my findings that he with dishonest intention prejudice the economic or financial interest of the State vis-a-vis Bangladesh Shilpa Bank "dishonestly removed the machineries of the Decent Oil Mill Ltd. during the period of attachment and misappropriated the same." 

 5. In this case after a preliminary enquiry on the basis of the complaint Ext. 4 dated 15.1.82 by P.W. 1 Mr. Karim, the then Manager of the Pabna Branch of the Shilpa Bank P.W.8 Dabiruddin, the then Assistant Inspector, District Anti-Corruption Bureau lodged F.I.R. Ext.10 with Pabna P.S. on 31.3.83 giving rise to D.A.B.G.R. case No. 7 of 1983 in the court of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Sadar, Pabna. Informant P.W.8 Dabiruddin, Assistant Inspector, District Anti-Corruption Bureau submitted charge-sheet against the accused appellant under sections 405 and 420 of the Penal Code on 29.6.83 showing him as absconder. Thereafter the accused appellant was produced in the Court of the said Sub-Divisional Magistrate under arrest on 29.10.83 and as his prayer for bail was rejected on several occasions he continued to remain in jail custody till some time between 11.7.85 and 3.8.85 when he was released on bail. When the police submitted supplementary charge sheet under the Special Powers Act, the case was sent to the Special Tribunal, Pabna who took cognizance of the offence under sections 15 and 16 of the Special Powers Act on 17.9.85, but allowed the accused to continue to remain on bail On 18.11.85 an application being Criminal Revision No. 137 of 1985 under section 561A Cr.P.C. for quashing the Criminal Proceedings against the accused was moved before a Division Bench of this court at Rangpur but the said application was summarily rejected on 18.11.85. The Special Tribunal started the trial of the accused in absentia on 8.12.86 and concluded the trial by passing a judgment and order on 7.2.86 convicting and sentencing the accused as aforesaid. Thereafter accused appellant surrendered before the Special Tribunal Pabna on 7.4.87 prayed for a copy of the judgment free of cost and also prayed for bail. The Special Tribunal rejected the prayer for bail, took him into custody and directed the official to supply a copy of the judgment to the convicted accused as per rules. Thereafter the assumed appellant Md. Anwar Ali while remaining in jail custody executed power in favour of the learned Advocate Mr. Joynal Abedin and then this appeal was filed in this court on 2.5.87 with a prayer for condo nation of delay of 53 days in filing the appeal. The delay was condoned and the appeal was admitted on 4.5.87. On behalf of accused appellant a prayer for bail was moved on 6.5.87 attaching a letter dated 8.3.87 from the Assistant General Manager, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank addressed to appellant Md. Anwar Ali. In the said letter dated 8.3.87 Mr. M.A. Quayum, Assistant General Manager, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank informed accused Anwar Ali that the Shilpa Bank has agreed to settle the dues on payment of the principal amount of Tk. 2,35,68/- if he pays the said amount in two equal installments on 30.6.87 and 30.12.87 waiving the interest subject to formal approval of the Government and the accused would be permitted to run the Textile unit on the land of Decent Oil Mill Ltd. if he executed an equitable mortgage of the Textile Printing and Finishing Project in favour of Bangladesh Shilpa Bank as early as possible. In the petition it was stated on hehalf of the accused-appellant that as the machineries could not be repaired (at Khulna), the said machineries had been brought back and were lying within the Decent Oil Mill Ltd. premises. It was also stated that the accused-appellant who is a "freedom fighter" of Bangladesh suffered from infirmity as he lost his left fore arm in the war of liberation. Mrs. Nurunnahar Begum, the wife of the accused in her petition Ext.6 dated 25.1.86 to the Managing Director, Shilpa Bank, however, had stated that her husband's left hand was amputated in the hospital after an accident. It was further stated that the accused never misappropriated the machineries of the Oil Mill that as the same could not be repaired, they have been brought back and are still lying within the Decent Oil Mill premises and that the present criminal case was started against him to coerce the accused-appellant to pay the Bank's dues on account of the Oil Mill and that as the negotiation between the accused and the Shilpa Bank was going on regarding the terms of settlement, it was agreed between the Shilpa Bank and the appellant that the criminal case would not be proceeded with and would be kept in abeyance till the payment is made by the appellant. The appellant bonafide believing that the criminal case is not being proceeded with, did not take any step in the criminal case and that he was surprised to learn on 5.4.87 that he was tried in absentia and convicted on 7.2.87. A learned Single Judge of this court on 13.5 .87 allowed the accused ad interim bail till 7.7.87 on condition that he complies with the Shilpa Bank's letter dated 8.3.87 by paying half of the principal amount of Tk. 2,35,681/- within 30.6.87 and the remaining half within 30.12.87; but the accused-appellant could not pay the first installment within 30.6.87 and instead of surrendering to the jail custody on 8.7.87 Mr. Joynal Abedin the learned Advocate for the appellant prayed for extending the period of bail. The prayer was rejected by this court and the accused appellant was directed to surrender to custody at once. The accused-appellant then on 29.8.87 surrendered in the court of District Magistrate, Pabna who took him into custody and thereafter this court on 31.8.81 has heard the learned Advocates for the appellant and the State while hearing the appeal on merit. 

 6. Mr. Mainul Hossain, the learned Advocate for the appellant in this court has read over the evidence on record and the judgment of the trial court. He has submitted that the accused appellant prayed for being added as a party in the court of the District Judge in Misc. Case No. 40 of 1978 but his prayer was arbitrarily rejected. He further submitted that the District Judge passed the ex-parte judgment beyond the knowledge of the accused, that the accused and his wife after purchasing all the shares of the previous owners of the Decent Oil Mill Ltd., acted bonafide arid in good faith in the interest of the Oil Mill by sending the machineries for repairing to Khulna as they were totally out of order and unfit for any use, that he informed this fact duly to the Shilpa Bank in writing, that when the Manager P.W.1 Mr. Karim and the local legal Advisor P.W. 6 Mr. Razzak, Advocate came to the Decent Oil Mill premises, the accused told them that the machineries were sent to Khulna for repair, that thereafter the Bank or the said officers of the Bank never told him to bring the machineries back to the Oil Mill without repairing immediately, that they also did not put the decree into execution and that to the surprise of the accused they started this false case of theft and misappropriation only to put pressure upon the accused to pay the dues of the Shilpa Bank and to harass the accused by putting him in jail for a long period financially ruining him. He submits that the prosecution has totally failed to prove the charge of misappropriation or theft of the machineries against the accused and has also not been able to prove that accused committed any prejudicial act to prejudice the economic and financial interest of the State vis-a-vis the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank established under P.O. No. 129 of 1972. 

 "In the said President's Order (P.O. No. 129 of 1972) special provisions have been made for speedy recovery of dues from the defaulter in articles 33, 34 and 35 of the said order. The loan is advanced on certain terms and conditions and loanee is under contractual obligation to repay the loan with interest in terms of the loan. In case of the breach of the obligation to repay the loan the Bank may take recourse to the said articles 33, 34 and 35 to recover the loan. The liability of the loanee is thus civil in nature." 

 But the liability of the loanees to repay the secured N being civil in nature, he can not be convicted u/s. 16 read with section 2(f) (viii) of the Special Powers Act merely for default in this payment of loan. Appropriate remedy for the Shilpa Bank is to take action under Article 33 or 34 or 35 of P.O. No. 129 of 1972. Be that as it may, on a reading of the evidence on record I find that only P.W. 1 Mr. Karim, the Manager Shilpa Bank, Dhaka and P.W.6 Mr. Razzak, a local Advocate and the legal Advisor of the Pabna Branch of the Shilpa Bank deposed that when they visited the Decent Oil Mill, they found no machineries and that on query accused appellant Anwar Ali told that he had sent the machineries to Khulna for repair. In the letter Ext.3/2 accused appellant Anwar Ali himself had informed the Manager (P.W.I Mr. Karim) of the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank, Motijheel C/A., Dhaka in writing that the factory building and its godown were damaged by the cyclone, that the previous owners and the Management of the Decent Oil Mill Ltd. even after 15 years of the import of the machineries failed to use or put them into operation with the help of the local experts and technicians and even the scientists of the Science Laboratory, Dhaka failed to assemble or modify the machineries, that the accused arranged to pay Tk. 55,000/- to the Shilpa Bank to clear a part of the principal amount of loan and would make further payment to repay the entire principal amount of loan on final settlement with the Shilpa Bank, that in the meanwhile the accused has re-constructed the factory building and godown and erected the boundary wall of the factory area and in the interest of the Oil Mill had sent the machineries of the Oil Mill for repairing and modification. On receiving this letter Ext. 3/2 of the accused, P.W.1 Mr. Karim, the Manager of the Shilpa Bank came from Dhaka for inspection of the Oil Mill. P.W.I Mr. Karim, Manager of the Shilpa Bank has stated in his evidence that the Shilpa Bank started Misc. Case No. 40 of 1978 in the Court of the District Judge, Pabna against the Decent Oil Mill and its previous owners (i.e., the Directors) and that the machineries were attached. It is admitted that the accused appellant and his wife purchased all the shares of the previous owners of the said Mill in the month of February, 1979. P.W.I Mr. Karim has also deposed, "Anwar Ali (accused) applied for being added as a party in that case; but it was rejected. Said Anwar Ali contacted me on 29.1.81 with Bank draft of Tk. 50,000/- (actually) two bank drafts-one of Tk. 55,000/- and another of Tk. 5,000/-) which I forwarded to the Head Office Head Office wrote this letter dated 9.3.83 (Ext.3/1) to accused Anwar Ali......... we hen visited the Decent Oil Mill and found no machineries. On query Anwar Ali gave out that he sent the machineries to Khulna for repair. Anwar Ali wrote this letter Ext.3/2 to Head Office." P.W.6 Mr. Razzak also stated similarly that the prayer of the accused to be added as a party in Misc. Case No. 40 of 1978 was rejected and that when he visited the Mill with the Manager and met the accused, the latter told them that he had sent the machineries, to Khulna for repair. Nobody including P.W.I and P.W.6 asked accused Anwar Ali the name and address of the repairing firm, factory or shop of Khulna where he had sent them for repair. They also did not ask him to bring the machineries to the Oil Mill immediately without delaying for repair. Neither P.W.1 and P.W. 6 or the Shilpa Bank asked him to bring the machineries or asked him to supply the name and address of the repairing firm. The Police also did not investigate this case in this direction. The accused appellant has asserted that the said machineries in spite of his best efforts could not be repaired and are now lying in the premises of the Decent Oil Mill. Anyway even if the entire evidence on record is believed, the only thing that has been proved by the said prosecution witnesses in this case is that the accused appellant informed the prosecution witnesses P.W.1 that he had sent the machineries of the Oil Mill to Khulna for repair and that the accused had informed the Manager of Head Office of the Shilpa Bank, Dhaka by his letter Ext.3/2 about the said fact. There is no allegation that the accused sold away or disposed of the mortgaged and attached machineries. From the evidence on record it cannot be inferred or held that the-accused appellant had misappropriated the said mortgaged and attached machineries or has committed theft of the said machineries with any dishonest intention though it is true that since the machineries are attached by the Court any subsequent sale of the same, if any, is void and purely by virtue of purchase of the shares of the Oil Mill, the accused has not acquired any right, title and interest in the machineries. On the other hand, from the evidence it appears reasonable to infer that the accused acted bonafide in the interest of the Oil Mill by trying to get the machineries repaired at Khulna. So it cannot be said that accused appellant committed any prejudicial act which was intended or likely to prejudice the economic of financial interest of a statutory public authority, namely, the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank which comes within the ambit of the expression "the State" by legal fiction as defined in Article 152(1) of the Constitution. The accused appellant is, therefore, entitled to be acquitted of the said charge. 

 In the result, the appeal is allowed. The order of conviction and sentence passed against him under section 16(3) of the Special Powers Act is set aside. He is acquitted of the charge under section 16(3) read with section 16(1)(a) of the Special Powers Act. He may be set at liberty at once if not wanted in any other case.
